You are a worker in the Fortress revival repo at /home/user/fortress (read CLAUDE.md briefly for orientation). Your task: characterize how the Fortress BYTECODE COMPILER path handles our revival-era test programs, versus the interpreter ("walk") path. The purpose is twofold: find potential performance wins, and catalog compiler gaps precisely so they can be prioritized later — the gap catalog grounded in real programs is the main deliverable.

Environment setup (required before any fortress command):
  export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
  export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
  export FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress
  unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS

Background you MUST read first:
- explorations/repo-internals.md — the compiler-path recipe, cache anatomy, and the stale-cache trap (a misleading NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println fixed by wiping default_repository/caches/* and compiling library components in order). Follow its recipe exactly.
- explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md — prior findings on the compiled path (it works on simple programs; imported library components like System and CompilerSystem must be explicitly `fortress compile`d into the cache first; the compiler is incomplete and fails on some constructs with `sayWhat` errors).

Interpreter usage for comparison: `./bin/fortress <file>.fss` runs a component whose name equals the filename sans .fss. Compiled path: see repo-internals.md (roughly `./bin/fortress compile <file>.fss` then `./bin/fortress run <component>`, after compiling required library components into the cache).

Targets, in this order (all in explorations/):
1. A trivial control: write your own tiny hello-style component in the scratchpad dir (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/), copy it into explorations/ temporarily if the tool requires repo-relative paths, to prove your compiled-path setup works end to end before judging anything else. Remove any temp file you add to explorations/ when done.
2. explorations/micrograd.fss — v1 scalar autodiff + XOR training (uses List library, objects with var fields, seq loops).
3. explorations/mgnative_a.fss — adds user opr juxtaposition/^ on objects, user BIG OPLUS registered via MonoidReduction + Comprehension + __bigOperatorSugar, SUM comprehensions, list comprehensions.
4. explorations/mgnative_b.fss — adds trait comprises (sealed ADT), multimethod dispatch, prefix opr DEL.
5. explorations/mgnative_c.fss — adds recursive prefix operator, tuples in Lists.
6. explorations/nprobe.fss and explorations/tparallel.fss — further idiom coverage.

For EACH target record: (a) does `compile` succeed — if not, the EXACT error, the construct that triggered it (quote the source line), and the compiler phase if identifiable (parse/typecheck/codegen `sayWhat`); (b) if it compiles, does `run` produce output identical to the interpreter run; (c) if it runs, wall-clock timing vs the interpreter on the same machine — run BOTH with FORTRESS_THREADS=1 for comparability and note the default-threads number too if interesting. The training programs print PASS lines and loss trajectories — compare those. Runs can take minutes; use generous timeouts (up to 10 minutes each).

Discipline: do NOT modify any tracked file. Do NOT commit or push anything. Work in the scratchpad for temp files. If caches get corrupted, the wipe-and-recompile recipe in repo-internals.md is the fix; wiping default_repository/caches/* is allowed (it is gitignored and rebuildable).

Deliverable: write a detailed report to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/compiled-path-report.md — a per-target table (compiles? runs? output matches? timings) followed by a gap catalog: each distinct compiler failure once, with the minimal construct that triggers it and the exact error text. If a failure looks like it might have a small workaround (e.g. an import difference), note it but do not rewrite our sources. Your final message: a compact summary of the table and the gap list, and the report path.

95	## The two worlds
96	
97	The tree contains two nearly-disjoint executions of Fortress, and most
98	confusion comes from mixing them up:
99	
100	| | interpreter ("walk") | bytecode compiler |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| era | 2003-lineage, mature | 2010–2012, the team's final push, incomplete |
103	| entry | `fortress <file>.fss` | `fortress compile <file>.fss` + `fortress run <component>` |
104	| libraries | `Library/` + `LibraryBuiltin/` (FortressBuiltin, NativeArray, ...) | `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra`, `CompilerSystem`, `GeneratorLibrary` |
105	| native mechanism | `builtinPrimitive("com.sun...glue.prim.X")` in .fss | `import java com.sun...nativeHelpers.{...}` in .fss |
106	| native String type | glue-level FString | `CompilerBuiltin.JavaString` / `StringVector` (foreign map in `NamingCzar`) |
107	| tests | `ProjectFortress/tests/` via `ant testSystem` | `compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` via `ant testFast` etc. |
108	
109	The mode switch is `com.sun.fortress.compiler.WellKnownNames`:
110	`useInterpreterLibraries()` / `useCompilerLibraries()` swap the meaning of
111	"the builtin library" (`FortressBuiltin` vs `CompilerBuiltin`) and "the
112	standard library" (`FortressLibrary` vs `CompilerLibrary`). `Shell.subMain`
113	calls one or the other per subcommand (`walk` vs `compile`/`run`/`link`).
114	
115	Consequences:
116	- A `.fss` file is generally written for ONE world. `import java ...` means
117	  compiler-only; `builtinPrimitive` means interpreter-only.
118	- An *api name* used by both worlds is trouble: apis resolve by name along a
119	  single shared source path (see below). This is exactly what broke the six
120	  interpreter tests in the 2012 endgame (`api System` shadowed — see
121	  test-baseline postscript) and why the compiler apis are `Compiler*`-prefixed.
122	
123	## Name resolution: fortress.source.path
124	
125	`default_repository/configuration` (overridable via `local_repository/`,
126	`~/.fortress/`, `./.fortress/`, env vars, or `-D` flags) defines:
127	
128	    fortress.source.path=;.;${_fr}/LibraryBuiltin;${FORTRESS_AUTOHOME}/Library;${_fr}/test_library
129	
130	- Leading `;` sets the separator (Windows compat). `.` (cwd!) is searched
131	  FIRST, then `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin`, then `Library/`.
132	- `import Foo` finds the first `Foo.fsi`/`Foo.fss` on that path. First hit
133	  wins — a file earlier on the path silently shadows a later one, and cwd can
134	  shadow everything (mind where you run from).
135	- The interpreter requires filename (sans suffix) == component/api name.
136	
137	## Cache anatomy and hygiene
138	
139	`default_repository/caches/` (gitignored):
140	- `analyzed_cache/`, `*parsed_cache/` — front-end analysis, shared-ish
141	  between worlds; the main source of cross-world contamination.
142	- `interpreter_cache/`, `environment_cache/` — interpreter side.
143	- `bytecode_cache/` — compiler output: one jar per compiled component;
144	  library components get api-qualified names (`fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`).
145	- `nativewrapper_cache/` — generated wrappers for `import java` natives.
146	
147	Rules learned the hard way:
148	- **When in doubt, wipe**: `rm -rf default_repository/caches/*`. Stale or
149	  order-inconsistent caches produce *misleading* runtime errors
150	  (`NoSuchMethodError: CompilerBuiltin.println(...)`,
151	  `NoSuchMethodError: ...asJavaString()`, `Unable to read serialized data
152	  ... recommend you delete the Fortress bytecode cache and relink`). These
153	  sank pluckyporcupine's compiler verdict; they are cache problems, not
154	  compiler bugs.
155	- After editing any `Library/`/`LibraryBuiltin/` `.fss`, wipe — edits are
156	  otherwise invisible (cached analysis wins).
157	- **Compile order matters** on a fresh cache, because `fortress compile` of a
158	  program does NOT emit the builtin-library jars, and the runtime classloader
159	  then falls back to the **bootstrap stubs** in `ProjectFortress/build/fortress/`
160	  (ant-compiled from checked-in `ProjectFortress/src/fortress/*.java` —
161	  a *frozen, older* snapshot of CompilerBuiltin!). Symptom: NoSuchMethodError
162	  on a method that plainly exists in CompilerBuiltin.fss. Recipe:
163	
164	      cd ProjectFortress
165	      ../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss
166	      ../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss
167	      ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss
168	      ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss
169	      ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss
170	      ../bin/fortress compile <program>.fss
171	      ../bin/fortress run <component> [args...]
172	
173	  The JUnit harness gets this right because `CompilerJUTest` starts with
174	  `Shell.resetRepository()` and compiles the world in dependency order.
175	
176	## Toolchain traps (JDK rungs)
177	
178	- **build.xml's javac tasks originally set `source=` but never `target=`**
179	  (and three set neither). Harmless on JDK 8 (target defaulted to 8); on
180	  JDK 11 target defaulted to 11 → v55 classfiles with invokedynamic string
181	  concat → ASM 3.1's ClassReader (used by `ForeignJava.findClass` for every
182	  `import java ...`) dies with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, failing all
183	  compiler-path tests while testSystem stays green. Fixed by pinning
184	  `target="${javaSourceVersion}"` on all 8 javac tasks (commit fdd4a57c2).
185	  Diagnosis trick: a 20-line probe compiling against
186	  `third_party/asm/asm-all-3.1.jar` + `javap -v | grep major` pinpoints
187	  exactly which classfile ASM chokes on. (Surprise: JDK 11's *platform*
188	  classes parse fine under `SKIP_DEBUG|SKIP_FRAMES|SKIP_CODE`; it was our
189	  own freshly compiled v55 output that broke.)
190	- `default_repository/caches/global.map` is a **tracked** file at the caches
191	  root, so `rm -rf default_repository/caches/*` deletes tracked content —
192	  wipe with `rm -rf default_repository/caches/*_cache
193	  default_repository/caches/logs` instead, or `git checkout` it back.
194	
195	## Generated code
196	
197	- AST nodes (`src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/`, 1000+ files),
198	  `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`, `Library/FortressAst.fsi/fss` are all
199	  generated by astgen from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast` (build
200	  target `makeAST`). They are checked in; ant's uptodate check compares
201	  mtimes, so a fresh checkout looks current. If scalac errors show arity
202	  mismatches in `S*Pattern` nodes: `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast
203	  && ant compileAll`.
204	- Parser (`parser/*.java` from Rats! grammars), `precedence_resolver/
205	  Operators.java` (from unicode data) — same pattern.
206	
207	## Test harness mechanics
208	
209	- Targets: `testFast` (unit + compiler suites, ~12 min, excludes interpreter
210	  system tests), `testSystem` (interpreter, 382 tests, ~2 min),
211	  `testLibrary`, `testCompiler`, `testNotPassing` (expected failures),
212	  `testDemos`, nightly variants. Plain-text results land in
213	  `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/TEST-<class>.txt`.
214	- `.test` files (in `compiler_tests/` etc.) are property files driving
215	  `FileTests`: keys like `compile`, `run`, `tests=`, `compile_err_equals=`
216	  decide which phases run and what output to expect. `run`-tests execute the
217	  compiled program via the `bin/run` script in a subprocess.
218	- To reproduce one interpreter test: `../bin/fortress tests/<Name>.fss`
219	  (from `ProjectFortress/`). Failures print the real diagnostic that the
220	  JUnit boilerplate hides.
221	- Suite runs reset/repopulate `default_repository/caches` — don't interleave
222	  ad-hoc compiles with a running suite, and don't trust cache state after one.
223	
224	## Git archaeology techniques
225	
226	- **The history has a parallel root**: `5a68404` (David Chase, 2012-07-19,
227	  4372 files) is a parentless import later merged by `575fe64`. Any
228	  `git log <base>..HEAD -- <file>` therefore lists `5a68404` for almost
229	  every file — useless for "who changed what since June". Use **content
230	  comparison** instead: `git diff --quiet <base> HEAD -- <file>` and
231	  `git show <base>:<file> | cmp - <other-tree>/<file>` (this is how the
232	  graft's 3-way audit was done; see the graft commit message).
233	- pluckyporcupine's base = trunk `304f274` (2012-06-12), confirmed by 56/69
234	  differing files being byte-identical to it.
235	- The twelve pre-2016 branches are hg named-branch relics; the 2008 research
236	  branches were squash-merged into trunk, so fine-grained authorship exists
237	  only on the branch heads. Full survey with per-branch verdicts: see the
238	  session notes / ask before deleting anything.
239	- hg conversion quirks: empty "Starting/Closing branch X" marker commits;
240	  `.hgignore` still in tree; David Chase's 2012-01-20 branch-closing sweep.

2	
3	First run of the 2012 test suite on the grafted tree (trunk `a874948` +
4	pluckyporcupine migration + build patches; branch tip `b598e0e`).
5	Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 container, OpenJDK 8u482, ant 1.10.14, Scala 2.10.7
6	(vendored). Commands: `ant testFast`, `ant testSystem`.
7	
8	## Results
9	
10	| suite | scope | result |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| `ant testFast` | 48 JUnit suites: unit tests + **CompilerJUTest (642)** + OtherCompilerJUTest (263) + LibraryJUTest (55) + ParserJUTest (188) | **all pass** (≈1,400 tests, 0 failures, ~12 min) |
13	| `ant testSystem` | 382 interpreter system tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/*.test`) | **375 pass, 7 fail** (~2 min) |
14	
15	Not yet run: `testNotPassing` (expected-failing), `testDemos`, `testsyntax`,
16	`testCruiseControl`/nightly variants.
17	
18	## The 7 interpreter failures — both causes understood
19	
20	**6 × `System` api shadowing** (`ParamRef`, `WordCountSmall`, `setMakerTest0`,
21	`LongStringTests`, `CovCollTest`, `FileConversion` — symptom:
22	`FortressBuiltin.JavaString/StringVector is undefined`):
23	the interpreter's original `Library/System.fsi` declares
24	`args : ImmutableArray[\String,ZZ32\]`, but David Chase's 2012-07-19 import
25	(`5a68404`) added a minimal, compiler-oriented
26	`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/System.fsi` (getProperty only), and
27	LibraryBuiltin shadows Library for the interpreter. **Pre-existing on the 2012
28	trunk, not a graft regression** — Chase's own merge commit `575fe64`
29	(2012-07-19) says: "merged, failing some tests that I think are irrelevant (at
30	least under 1.7)". pluckyporcupine's June-12 base predates the shadowing file,
31	so their tree passes these — at the cost of lacking the July compiler work.
32	Candidate fix: extend `LibraryBuiltin/System.fsi/fss` to cover the original
33	api surface (`args`, `programName`, ...).
34	
35	**1 × `realArith`** — float-printing last digit:
36	`a Float: 2.718281828459045 =/= a FloatLiteral: 2.7182818284590455`.
37	JDK-era artifact (double parse/print behavior differs from the 2012 JDK 6/7
38	toolchain); harmless but should be understood before the JDK 11 rung.
39	
40	## Major discovery: the bytecode compiler path WORKS on JDK 8
41	
42	pluckyporcupine's README says "The compiler works, but running compiled
43	programs does not." **On JDK 8 that is false.** Verified end-to-end:
44	
45	```bash
46	cd ProjectFortress
47	../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/System.fss      # native-backed lib deps
48	../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss  # must be compiled once
49	../bin/fortress compile hello.fss
50	../bin/fortress run hello one two three
51	# fortress.home is  /home/user/fortress
52	# Hello, World!
53	# one
54	# three
55	# two        <- out of order: Fortress `for` loops are implicitly PARALLEL
56	```
57	
58	All 642 `CompilerJUTest` tests (including the 52 `.test` files that compile
59	*and execute* programs via `bin/run`) pass.
60	
61	Two traps that produced the historical "compiler is broken" verdict:
62	
63	1. **Stale caches.** With leftover state in `default_repository/caches/`,
64	   compiled programs die with
65	   `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)` — byte-for-byte
66	   pluckyporcupine's NOTES.md error (they saw it on Java 9; we reproduced it
67	   on JDK 8 before wiping caches). Fresh caches (`rm -rf
68	   default_repository/caches/*`, then recompile; the JUnit harness does
69	   `Shell.resetRepository()`) make it vanish. Their failure was plausibly
70	   this, not Java 9.
71	2. **Imported library components are not auto-compiled.** A program importing
72	   `System` / `CompilerSystem` needs those compiled into the bytecode cache
73	   first (errors: `Resource not found: System.class`,
74	   `NoClassDefFoundError: CompilerSystem$args`).
75	
76	Remaining truth in the old caveat: `hello.fss` still cannot run on the
77	*interpreter* (its imports resolve into the compiler-path library surface),
78	and the compiler still rejects constructs the 2012 team hadn't finished
79	(e.g. pluckyporcupine hit "mutable bindings not yet handled" on other
80	programs). The compiler is *incomplete*, not *broken*.

83	
84	Both failure classes were fixed the next day — the suite is now fully green:
85

92	  `../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`, `../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss`,
93	  `../Library/CompilerSystem.fss` — then the program. See
94	  `repo-internals.md` for why the order matters.
95	- `realArith`: the `e` constant in `Library/Constants.fss` was hand-tuned to
96	  the 2012 JDK's `exp(1.0)` (1 ulp above correctly-rounded e); corrected to
97	  the double nearest e (commit "Correct the e constant").
98

100	
101	The grafted tree is healthier than either parent lineage: it carries the full
102	Aug-2012 feature state, compiles under JDK 8, passes the entire unit/compiler
103	suite, and 98% of the interpreter suite, with all 7 failures explained (6
104	pre-existing upstream, 1 JDK-era cosmetic).
